title: Bank of Mexico Surprises and Cuts Interest Rate to 6.25%
author: Braulio Carbajal
content:
_This article by[Braulio
Carbajal](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Braulio%20Carbajal) originally
appeared in the [November 5, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/11/05/economia/banco-de-
mexico-sorprende-y-baja-la-tasa-de-interes-a-625), Mexico's premier left wing
daily newspaper._

**Mexico City**. The Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico (BdeM) decided by
majority to **lower by a quarter of a percentage point** the target for [the
overnight interbank interest
rate](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/09/24/economia/banco-de-mexico-
mantiene-tasa-de-interes-en-65), which stood at **6.25 percent** effective
November 6, after judging that the disinflationary process has continued and
that no demand pressures are perceived in the economy.

Victoria Rodríguez Ceja, José Gabriel Cuadra García and Omar Mejía Castelazo
voted in favor of the cut. Galia Borja Gómez and Jonathan Heath came out in
favor of keeping the rate at 6.50 percent. The decision was made with all
members of the Board present, which described it as a one-time adjustment.

The central bank noted that in the third quarter of 2026 the economy continued
to expand.

Between the first half of September and the first half of October, [headline
inflation](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/10/22/economia/inflacion-
subio-a-362-en-la-primera-quincena-de-octubre-afectada-por-alza-de-
energeticos) rose from 3.42 to **3.62 percent** , the result of an increase in
non-core inflation. Core inflation fell marginally from 3.79 to 3.78 percent
in that period.

Headline inflation forecasts were revised upward for the fourth quarter of
2026, mainly due to higher-than-anticipated levels of non-core inflation. For
that quarter the BdeM projects 3.7 percent for headline inflation, compared
with 3.5 forecast on September 24, and 3.7 for core, compared with 3.6.

The expectation that headline inflation will **converge to the target in the
fourth quarter of 2027** is maintained. For the four quarters of 2027 the
central bank forecasts headline inflation of 3.4, 3.3, 3.2 and 3.0 percent,
unchanged from its September estimate, and core inflation with the same
trajectory. These forecasts, the central bank specified, are subject to
various risks.

As upside risks for inflation, the Board pointed to the persistence of core
inflation, a greater [depreciation of the
peso](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/11/05/economia/recorte-del-bdem-
presiona-al-peso-cotiza-a-1877-por-dolar), disruptions from trade policies or
an inflationary impact from geopolitical conflicts, climate effects and cost
pressures.

On the other hand, as downside risks it identified lower-than-anticipated
economic activity in Mexico and the United States, a smaller pass-through of
cost increases and lower pressures associated with episodes of appreciation of
the national currency. It estimated that the balance of risks maintains an
upward bias.

In the external environment, the document states that global economic activity
would have expanded in the third quarter at a slightly slower pace than in the
previous quarter. In several advanced economies headline inflation continued
to rise due to higher energy prices.

## Fed Kept Its Rates Unchanged

[The Federal Reserve kept
unchanged](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/10/28/economia/fed-
mantiene-tasas-de-interes-aplaza-modificacion-hasta-despues-de-elecciones-
legislativas-de-eu) the federal funds rate range at its October meeting, and
U.S. government rates declined at most maturities, although long-term rates
reached multi-decade highs.

International financial markets continued to be volatile, the dollar showed
limited variations and uncertainty persists over the conflict in the Middle
East and its repercussions.

Since the previous decision, rates on government securities in Mexico fell at
medium and long maturities and rose at short ones, while the Mexican peso
depreciated. Economic policy changes by the U.S. administration and the
possible prolongation of geopolitical conflicts, the Board noted, add
uncertainty to the forecasts and could generate pressures on inflation in both
directions.

Going forward, the central bank considers that **keeping the rate at the level
reached for a prolonged period** will support the convergence of inflation to
its target and will be adequate to face external macroeconomic challenges. Its
decisions will take into account the observed and expected behavior of
inflation, as well as the pass-through of the exchange rate to consumer
prices.

The BdeM reaffirmed its commitment to its priority mandate and to the need to
persevere in its efforts to consolidate an environment of low and stable
inflation.
